The STATdx rendering is selected for default download so the complete STATdx sequence remains contiguous; the RadPrimer rendering is archive-optional for traceability/recovery. === DIFFERENTIAL DIAGNOSIS === - [RadPrimer] Common: Hepatic cyst; autosomal dominant polycystic disease, liver; hepatic pyogenic abscess; biliary hamartomas; hepatic metastases; hepatic amebic abscess; biloma/seroma; steatosis/fatty liver mimic. - [RadPrimer] Less common: Hepatic candidiasis; hepatic hydatid cyst; biliary cystadenoma/carcinoma; biliary intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm; hepatocellular carcinoma; Caroli disease; undifferentiated hepatic sarcoma; intrahepatic pseudocyst; hepatic inflammatory pseudotumor; ciliated hepatic foregut cyst. === HIGH-YIELD DISCRIMINATORS === - [Both] Mural nodularity, enhancing wall/septa, internal debris, high-attenuation blood, bile-duct communication, and interval change are the main discriminators for cystic hepatic masses. - [Both] Compare with prior studies: simple cysts change size slowly, abscesses can change quickly, and treated tumors such as GIST metastases may become cystic and simulate benign cysts. - [Both] Multiplanar review matters: coronal and sagittal imaging can reveal morphology, true lesion number, biliary communication, daughter cysts, or surgical/traumatic context. - [Both] A lesion that looks cystic but has a mural nodule, solid component, arterial hyperenhancement/washout, enhancing septa, or ductal surface nodularity should be treated as tumor until proven otherwise. - [Both] Clinical setting is decisive for infection and collections: fever/immunosuppression suggests abscess/candidiasis; trauma, surgery, ablation, or transplant suggests biloma/seroma; endemic exposure plus serology supports hydatid or amebic disease. - [Both] Steatosis is an important mimic: focal fat can approach water attenuation on noncontrast CT, but US echogenicity and opposed-phase MR signal dropout distinguish it from a true cystic mass. === DIAGNOSIS-SPECIFIC SYNTHESIS === - [Both] Hepatic cyst: Water attenuation, no visible wall, no enhancement, no mural nodularity, very bright T2/dark T1 signal, and sonolucent US with acoustic enhancement. One or two thin septa may occur. Hemorrhage can make a benign cyst difficult to separate from cystic neoplasm. Use STATdx images 1-3 for uncomplicated, obstructing, and hemorrhagic cyst variants. - [Both] Autosomal dominant polycystic disease of the liver: Numerous cysts of varying size can produce massive hepatomegaly but rarely impair liver function. Diagnosis is not made from liver cysts alone; look for cysts in other organs, family history, or genetic testing. Use STATdx image 4 for the core pattern. - [Both] Hepatic pyogenic abscess: Multiloculated/multiseptate complex cyst cluster with enhancing wall or septa; peripheral lesions near the diaphragm may have adjacent atelectasis or pleural effusion. Etiologies include surgery/trauma, cholecystitis/cholangitis, or hematogenous spread from colon. Use STATdx image 5 for complex abscess with aspiration/drainage context. - [Both] Biliary hamartomas: Innumerable small low-attenuation lesions that mimic cysts on CT/MR, often 1-1.5 cm, sometimes with echogenic or enhancing wall nodules. Lack of larger cystic lesions and lack of extrahepatic cysts helps distinguish them from polycystic liver disease. Use STATdx images 6-8 as a CT/US/MRCP multimodality cluster. - [Both] Hepatic metastases: Cystic metastases may arise from cystic primaries such as ovarian tumor, squamous cell metastases, mucinous adenocarcinoma, sarcomas, or treated GIST. Mural nodularity on CT, US, or MR is a key clue. Use STATdx image 9 for a cystic thyroid metastasis with mural nodule and STATdx images 10-11 as an atomic gastric GIST treatment-response cluster. - [Both] Hepatic amebic abscess: Typically solitary, peripheral, round or ovoid, and diagnosis usually rests on imaging plus clinical presentation and serology. Use STATdx image 12 for the classic shaggy encapsulated cystic mass. - [Both] Biloma/seroma: Occurs after trauma, partial liver resection, or radiofrequency ablation; uninfected collections may not require drainage and may take weeks to months to resolve. In a liver allograft, biloma from hepatic artery thrombosis with biliary necrosis is ominous. Use STATdx image 13 for posttraumatic biloma/seroma and STATdx images 14-15 as the transplant hepatic-artery-thrombosis cluster. - [Both] Hepatic candidiasis: Innumerable microabscesses, often less than 1 cm, with target or wheel appearance in immunocompromised patients; fungal and mycobacterial opportunistic infection may overlap. Use STATdx image 16. - [Both] Hepatic hydatid cyst: Solitary or multiple cysts with discrete peripheral wall with or without calcification; mother cyst contains hydatid matrix/sand and daughter cysts or scolices. Use STATdx image 17. - [Both] Biliary cystadenoma/carcinoma: Usually a solitary, large, multiseptate mass with enhancing wall and septa, classically in middle-aged women. Complete resection is essential to prevent recurrence. Use STATdx image 18. - [Both] Biliary intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm: Bile-duct tumor can produce mucin that distends ducts and simulates a cystic mass; nodular enhancing components raise concern for cholangiocarcinoma. Use STATdx image 19. - [Both] Hepatocellular carcinoma: Spontaneous or treatment necrosis can simulate a cystic mass; solid arterial hyperenhancing components and delayed washout point back to HCC. No selected source image uniquely illustrates HCC in this bundle, so retain as a text differential. - [Both] Caroli disease: Cystic intrahepatic bile-duct dilation communicates with bile ducts; MRCP or ERCP is recommended, and central dot sign reflects dilated ducts around portal vein radicles. Use STATdx image 20. - [Both] Undifferentiated hepatic sarcoma: Rare aggressive primary hepatic tumor, usually a very large solitary encapsulated mass with peripheral hypervascular solid component, complex cystic spaces, focal hemorrhage, and possible paradoxical solid US/cystic CT-MR appearance from myxoid stroma. Use STATdx image 21. - [Both] Intrahepatic pseudocyst and hepatic inflammatory pseudotumor: Pseudocyst can dissect along portal triads and should prompt search for pancreatitis or adjacent pancreatic cyst; inflammatory pseudotumor more often mimics cholangiocarcinoma with delayed enhancement but rarely appears multiseptate/cystic. Retain as text differentials unless later images are supplied. - [Both] Ciliated hepatic foregut cyst: Rare congenital cyst, typically small and in segment IV, that may appear complex or solid on US. Use STATdx image 22. === SELECTED PRIMARY IMAGE SET === - STATdx image 1: Axial CECT in a 79-year-old woman shows a spherical liver mass with water density, homogeneous contents. No internal debris or wall irregularities are present. Used for: simpleHepaticCyst, waterDensity, noWallNodularity, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 2: Axial CECT shows an unusually large, simple hepatic cyst that caused compression and obstruction of the intrahepatic bile ducts . Used for: largeSimpleHepaticCyst, biliaryObstruction, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 3: Axial T2 FS MR shows several large, contiguous hepatic cysts. Hemorrhage within the cysts accounts for decreased signal intensity within portions of the cysts . Used for: hemorrhagicHepaticCysts, T2SignalComplexity, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialT2FSMR. - STATdx image 4: Axial CECT shows innumerable hepatic cysts of water attenuation and varying size, causing hepatomegaly. Only a few small renal cysts are present, and renal function is normal. Used for: autosomalDominantPolycysticLiverDisease, hepatomegaly, multifocalWaterAttenuationCysts, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 5: Axial CECT shows a liver mass with innumerable septa and slightly higher than water density contents . Needle aspiration yielded a small quantity of pus, and a catheter was inserted for drainage. The etiology was subacute diverticulitis. Used for: hepaticPyogenicAbscess, multiloculatedAbscess, septa, drainageContext, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 6: Axial CECT in a 53-year-old man shows innumerable small, cystic lesions throughout the liver, ranging in size from 2-15 mm. The lesions are often not perfectly spherical, and many have visible nodular enhancement within their walls. Used for: biliaryHamartomas, innumerableSmallCysticLesions, nodularWallEnhancement, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 7: US shows only the lesions > 10 mm as cystic structures , while the smaller lesions are hyperechoic to background liver. All are typical features of biliary hamartomas. Used for: biliaryHamartomas, ultrasoundVariant, smallHyperechoicLesions, recognitionReinforcement, US. - STATdx image 8: Coronal MRCP shows innumerable small, T2-hyperintense lesions that do not communicate with the biliary tree. Used for: biliaryHamartomas, MRCPVariant, noncommunicatingT2HyperintenseLesions, recognitionReinforcement, coronalMRCP. - STATdx image 9: Axial CECT shows several hypodense hepatic masses, including 1 cystic lesion . The subtle mural nodule is the clue that this is a neoplasm (metastatic thyroid cancer). Used for: cysticHepaticMetastases, muralNodule, thyroidCancerMetastasis, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 10: Axial CECT shows a heterogeneous, solid mass in the left lobe (that subsequently underwent cystic necrosis with treatment). This was found to be metastatic gastric GIST. Used for: gastricGISTMetastasis, pretreatmentSolidMass, samePatientFollowUpCluster, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 11: Axial CECT shows a cystic lesion in the left lobe. This is a metastatic gastric GIST that responded to Gleevec therapy with complete necrosis. Used for: gastricGISTMetastasis, treatmentNecrosis, GleevecResponse, samePatientFollowUpCluster, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 12: Axial CECT shows a shaggy, encapsulated, solitary cystic mass with nonenhancing contents, representing a typical amebic abscess. The imaging appearance, clinical presentation, and serology usually suffice for diagnosis. Used for: hepaticAmebicAbscess, shaggyEncapsulatedCysticMass, clinicalSerologyCorrelation, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 13: Axial CECT 3 weeks after a blunt traumatic liver laceration shows a lobulated, cystic lesion that represents a combination of walled-off bile and blood, also known, respectively, as biloma and seroma. Clinical history and comparison with prior CT scans provide confident diagnosis. Used for: bilomaSeroma, postTraumaticLiverLaceration, walledOffBileBlood, historyComparison, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 14: Axial CECT shows an irregular cystic lesion within a transplanted liver. This is a biloma with biliary necrosis as a result of hepatic artery thrombosis. Used for: transplantBiloma, hepaticArteryThrombosis, biliaryNecrosis, sameProcessCluster, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 15: Axial CECT shows dilated bile ducts, peribiliary hepatic fluid, and a cystic biloma in a liver allograft, as a result of hepatic artery thrombosis. Used for: transplantBiloma, peribiliaryFluid, hepaticArteryThrombosis, sameProcessCluster, STATdxSupplementalImage, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 16: Axial CECT in a febrile, immune-suppressed patient shows innumerable small, hypodense lesions in the liver with irregular walls. Other opportunistic hepatic infections may have a similar appearance. Used for: hepaticCandidiasis, microabscesses, immunosuppressedPatient, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 17: Coronal CECT in immigrant from Middle East shows 2 large, multiseptate, cystic masses . Within outer pericyst are multiple daughter cysts or scolices. Imaging appearance, coupled with serology, is usually sufficient for diagnosis. Used for: hepaticHydatidCyst, daughterCysts, scolices, endemicTravelImmigrantContext, recognitionReinforcement, coronalCECT. - STATdx image 18: Coronal CECT in a middle-aged woman shows complex, cystic mass, lobulated margins, enhancing wall and septa . These findings with no other known tumor could be considered sufficiently diagnostic of biliary cystadenoma to warrant resection without further evaluation. Used for: biliaryCystadenomaCarcinoma, enhancingWallSepta, middleAgedWoman, resectionManagement, recognitionReinforcement, coronalCECT. - STATdx image 19: Axial CECT of biliary IPMN with cholangiocarcinoma shows dilated intrahepatic bile ducts and a cystic mass . ERCP showed opacification of the cyst with contrast and the presence of surface nodularity within the bile ducts. Used for: biliaryIPMN, cholangiocarcinomaConcern, bileDuctCommunication, surfaceNodularity, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 20: Axial CECT in a woman with portal hypertension due to congenital hepatic fibrosis and Caroli disease shows splenomegaly, varices , and multiple hepatic cysts. These represent dilated intrahepatic bile ducts, draped around the central dot of accompanying portal veins . Used for: CaroliDisease, centralDotSign, portalHypertension, dilatedIntrahepaticBileDucts, recognitionReinforcement, axialCECT. - STATdx image 21: Coronal CECT in a man with RUQ pain shows a huge, multiseptate, cystic mass with enhancing peripheral components. Intraperitoneal blood was due to capsular rupture of this undifferentiated primary hepatic sarcoma. Used for: undifferentiatedHepaticSarcoma, hugeMultiseptateCysticMass, capsularRuptureHemoperitoneum, recognitionReinforcement, coronalCECT. - STATdx image 22: Axial T2 MR in a 29-year-old woman with a solid-appearing mass on US shows a complex, cystic-appearing mass in segment 4 that had no enhancement on other sequences. Resection proved ciliated hepatic foregut cyst. Used for: ciliatedHepaticForegutCyst, segment4ComplexCyst, T2MRVariant, resectionProof, recognitionReinforcement, axialT2MR. === ARCHIVE-OPTIONAL DUPLICATE IMAGES === - RadPrimer image 1: archiveOptionalDuplicate. few renal cysts and normal renal function in caption keep diagnosis nuanced. - STATdx image 6, STATdx image 7, STATdx image 8: CT, US, and MRCP examples of biliary hamartomas should remain together as multimodality recognition reinforcement. - STATdx image 10, STATdx image 11: STATdx-only gastric GIST metastasis pair shows pretreatment solid metastasis and post-Gleevec cystic necrosis; preserve as an atomic follow-up/treatment-response cluster. - STATdx image 13: Trauma-history biloma/seroma example depends on interval context and comparison with prior CT scans. - STATdx image 14, STATdx image 15: STATdx-only transplant biloma examples both teach hepatic artery thrombosis with biliary necrosis/peribiliary fluid and should remain together. - STATdx image 17: Large multiseptate cysts with daughter cysts/scolices and endemic/immigrant context. - STATdx image 18, STATdx image 19: Biliary cystadenoma/carcinoma and biliary IPMN/cholangiocarcinoma concern both hinge on enhancing wall/septa, duct communication, or nodularity. - STATdx image 20, STATdx image 21, STATdx image 22: Caroli disease central-dot sign, undifferentiated hepatic sarcoma, and ciliated hepatic foregut cyst cover key less-common mimics that should remain selected. - RadPrimer duplicate renderings were archived only because the equivalent STATdx source-image sequence was selected as the complete curated primary set. === GENERATOR INSTRUCTIONS === - Use this package as source material for later narrative/cards, but do not generate cards or lecture output during this synthesis step. - Use clean source-qualified labels in prose, such as STATdx image 7; keep RP-05/SDX-07 codes in registry, filenames, traceability fields, and import JSON. - Download only selectedPrimaryImageIds by default; archiveOptionalImageIds are available for recovery/review and should not drive default cards or lectures. - Use canonicalHierarchy exactly as copied from metadata.json for deckPath and any IMAIOS breadcrumb routing. - Do not fabricate Core Radiology support;
